title: Is intrauterine exposure to acetaminophen associated with emotional and hyperactivity problems during childhood? Findings from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort.
ehr_evidence: We performed a prospective longitudinal population-based study using data from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort; exposure (acetaminophen use during pregnancy) was collected retrospectively via a standardized perinatal questionnaire and outcomes via the parent-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ).
summary: A prospective longitudinal population-based cohort study of 4231 children from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort examined the association between intrauterine acetaminophen exposure and emotional and hyperactivity/inattention problems at ages 6 and 11 years.
key_findings: At 6 years, acetaminophen use in boys was associated with increased odds of emotional problems (adjusted OR = 1.47; 95% CI: 1.07–2.02) and hyperactivity/inattention problems (adjusted OR = 1.42; 95% CI: 1.06–1.92).
At 11 years, the effect attenuated and lost significance after adjustment for boys: emotional problems OR = 1.31 (95% CI: 0.99–1.73) and hyperactivity/inattention OR = 1.25 (95% CI: 0.95–1.65).
No association was observed for any phenotypes at either age in girls.
No associations between acetaminophen exposure and total difficulties or SDQ subscales were observed after adjustment in the total sample.

Sensitivity analysis found no association between other nonsteroidal analgesics and emotional (adjusted OR = 1.09; 95% CI: 0.77–1.55) or hyperactivity (adjusted OR = 1.07; 95% CI: 0.77–1.48) symptoms.
captured_features: Maternal acetaminophen use during pregnancy (at least once vs never)

Maternal age, parity, national economic index, maternal educational level, smoking and alcohol use during pregnancy, maternal skin color, infections during pregnancy, pre-gestational BMI, maternal mood issues, use of other analgesics
population: Children from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort in southern Brazil, assessed at ages 6 (N=3470) and 11 (N=3447) years
exposure_domain: Prenatal medication exposure (acetaminophen/paracetamol use during pregnancy)
limitations: Retrospective recall of maternal medication use during pregnancy likely caused underreporting and exposure misclassification.
Data did not allow evaluation of exposure by trimester of pregnancy or dose.
Residual confounding by socioeconomic position variables could not be fully excluded.
No information on reasons for medication use (e.g., fever/infection) during pregnancy.
